description.text:
The promos of Japan's Diamond & Pearl years: 127 cards, 001/DP-P to 127/DP-P, released from late 2006 to January 2009. The run began alongside Space-Time Creation, the first DP expansion, when the promo suffix changed from PCG-P to DP-P, and most of its cards are reprints of expansion cards.

The biggest groups came with Meiji Chocolate and from the Trade Please DP trading events at Pokémon Centers and the World Hobby Fair. Others came in each expansion's Special Pack and Official Visual Book, with McDonald's and Domino's Pizza, as Pokémon anniversary commemorative cards, through the Collection Challenge campaign, and at Battle Road, the Winter Challenge and the tournament that chose Japan's World Championships players.

description.text:
Given with the December 2006 issue of CoroCoro Comic, on sale from 15 November 2006, to launch the Pokémon Card Game DP series. It is the first of the DP promos, the 127 numbered Japanese promos of the Diamond & Pearl era.

The card came attached to a mount in the magazine. Readers who brought the mount to the Pokémon Diamond & Pearl Battle Festa 2006 or to an official gym event that December could exchange it for Lucario 002/DP-P, Riolu's evolution, while stocks lasted. Kouki Saitou drew both cards.

Given in exchange for the mount that Riolu 001/DP-P came on in the December 2006 issue of CoroCoro Comic, so a reader could have both Riolu and its evolution. The exchange was at the Pokémon Card Game information corner of the Pokémon Diamond & Pearl Battle Festa 2006, held at four venues in the Kansai, Tokai, Kyushu and Kanto regions between 25 November and 17 December 2006 to celebrate the new Diamond & Pearl games and cards, and at official gym events that December, while stocks lasted.

Kouki Saitou drew it, as he drew the Riolu.

Given to every player of Battle Road Stadium DP, the main card tournament of the Pokémon Diamond & Pearl Battle Festa 2006, which toured four venues in the Kansai, Tokai, Kyushu and Kanto regions between 25 November and 17 December 2006 to celebrate the new Diamond & Pearl games and cards. Players brought 30-card decks and climbed three stages: two wins cleared the first, three wins in a row the second, and the last was a match against a researcher of the Pokémon Card Laboratory, the game's developers. Beating the researcher won a newly drawn Battle Road Stadium card.

Manaphy was also given at the Festa's Diamond & Pearl Double Experience corner. Atsuko Nishida drew it.

Came with the Pokémon Card Game DP Official Visual Book, which Media Factory published on 8 December 2006. Written by the Pokémon Card Laboratory, the book showed every card of the first Diamond & Pearl products, the entry pack, the random starter decks and the Space-Time Creation expansions, sorted by type, with a deck matrix, columns and the official rules. It came with this original holo card and a poster listing every card on its back.

Later DP and Platinum visual books came with holo cards of their own, starting with Garchomp LV.X 058/DP-P. Ryo Ueda drew this one.

One of eight promos from the Trade Please DP corner (とりかえっこDP) of the 25th Next Generation World Hobby Fair, which visited Osaka on 14 January, Tokyo on 20 and 21 January, Nagoya on 28 January and Fukuoka on 4 February 2007. Visitors swapped one Pokémon card of their own, even an old yellow-bordered card or one with the old card back, for one of the eight, Turtwig, Chimchar, Piplup, Pachirisu, Buneary, Mime Jr., Glameow and Staravia, without choosing which, while stocks lasted. Trainer and Energy cards could not be swapped.

Official gym events in January and February 2007 ran the same corner and gave the same cards in their knockout battles and lotteries. The eight came back at the Gym Challenge tournaments held to launch the Secret of the Lakes expansion and the Rampardos and Bastiodon half decks, played with 30-card decks: every player got three cards for a first match, two for a second and three for a third, win or lose. This one came with the first match. Masakazu Fukuda drew it.
